critique.observed: Three observed air-fryer listings and two observed meat-thermometer listings share one five-link front page.

critique.observed: The recorded destinations are observations; all intended-ASIN fields remain blank.

prompt_intro: Copy this prompt only after reviewing the questions and choosing the proposed page set. The five observed listing destinations are not confirmations of product intent. Event names, brand direction, cadence and architecture below are proposals; never turn them into facts.

prompt.label: Role and goal
prompt.text: Design and build a polished, reader-first Amazon affiliate publication for people comparing kitchen appliances. The goal is a useful shopping decision, not a compliance dashboard. Preserve the existing evidence discipline, make missing facts visible without turning the homepage into an audit, and never promise search rank, sales or income.

prompt.label: Products in scope — observed, not intended
prompt.text:
The current owner brief supplies five short links. The dated shop register records these observed destinations only; none is confirmed as the intended product. Keep each submitted URL, intended ASIN/official listing/date/source, and observed redirect target in separate fields.
1. https://link.amazon/B04G1MEwY → observed https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3 — CHEFMAN 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer Oven with Easy View Windows, Sync Finish, Hi-Fry, Auto Shutoff, 2 Independent 3Qt Nonstick Dishwasher Safe Frying Baskets, Digital Double Air Fryer - Black.

These are observations recorded on 2026-11-17, not current availability checks or confirmation of owner intent. Do not call the supplied short links invalid; their exact compliance status remains unresolved. Do not invent products or attributes.

prompt.label: Audience and product scope
prompt.text: Use a provisional reader: someone comparing a countertop kitchen appliance and wanting a clear question answered before leaving for the listing. Do not infer the target country, audience demographics, currency or marketplace from the owner’s current location or the observed Amazon.com destinations. The site currently spans air fryers and meat thermometers; present them as separate categories until the owner confirms the broader niche.

prompt.label: Brand and voice
prompt.text: Use “Zone3” only as the current working label. Final publisher name, domain/handle clearance, palette and voice are not confirmed. Write like a careful human editor: direct, specific, calm, and willing to say what a listing does not tell you. Avoid generic AI phrases, stacked hedges, fake urgency, superlatives without evidence and fictional first-person experience. Use a human byline only when the named person has actually reviewed the page.

prompt.label: Information architecture — recommended default, not yet selected
prompt.text: Recommended public structure: one root publication front page; /shop/ for distinct product/category destinations (Air fryers and Meat thermometers); /guides/ for question-led editorial; one clear “Research & governance” navigation group and a footer that keeps sources, decisions, flagged items and the campaign ledger reachable. Inventory unique content in /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ before merging, archiving or redirecting anything. Do not create another parallel shop or blog.

prompt.label: Visual system
prompt.text: Design direction: editorial kitchen journal, not admin dashboard. Warm paper/cream background, deep ink, restrained olive/sage and a single warm accent; editorial serif for display headings paired with a legible sans-serif for body copy; comfortable 17px body type, generous whitespace and a readable line length. Cards should feel like a magazine shelf, not KPI tiles. Use visible focus, semantic headings, adequate contrast, reduced-motion support and comfortable touch targets. The palette is a proposal until the publisher identity is chosen.

prompt.label: Buyer-facing components
prompt.text: Build a compact two-category chooser; product cards that show the official listing title, observed/intended status and a useful question; a comparison that includes only attributes verified from official pages; and a short “what to check before you choose” list. Every product card must say what the listing states and what it does not establish. Do not issue an overall winner or “fits you if” claim without a human-reviewed basis.

prompt.label: Affiliate links and disclosures
prompt.text: On every page, put the exact disclosure “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.” in a readable strip directly under the masthead and repeat it in the footer; keep disclosure near each recommendation. Mark every outbound product link rel="sponsored". State where the link goes. Do not silently replace the submitted short links or add a tracking redirect. The owner supplied shopnow047c-20, but do not embed it in rewritten links until account/marketplace and one Special Link destination/report test are verified. The supplied short links are unresolved, not declared invalid.

prompt.label: Evidence rules
prompt.text: Every product fact must link to the official page that supports it and retain a checked date. No official source means blank/“not verified”, with a visible flag. Never merge observed redirects with intended-product confirmation. Do not infer price, availability, rating, review count, popularity, trends, commission potential, conversion or revenue. Show price/rating/review content only through an approved Amazon-served link or permitted API data, after current policy and account access are verified. Do not send Amazon Program Content to AI/ML processing unless the current official policy and required written permission explicitly allow it.

prompt.label: Editorial engine and topic hypotheses
prompt.text: Use one buyer question per page, answer directly, show the source, explain the decision trade-off and link to the relevant category/comparison. The four supplied working titles are: “Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?”, “A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity”, “How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs”, and “Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance.” Add separate thermometer questions only after confirming category scope and sources. These are editorial hypotheses, not evidence of search popularity.

prompt.label: Seasons, bylines and imagery
prompt.text: Seasonal angles are hypotheses, never “trending” claims. Date each seasonal page, review it before the relevant season and maintain an expiry/recheck owner. Never invent an author, test, review or product experience. Do not use generated, scraped or copied product photography as genuine product photos. Use original owner-created photography with documented rights or a permitted Amazon image source; until rights/provenance are recorded, use typography and original diagrams instead.

prompt.label: Organic discovery and topic measurement
prompt.text: Build one distinct, useful guide per real buyer question. Give each page a unique title/description, canonical URL and purposeful internal links within its category. Keep the existing register-driven RSS feed and sitemap current on each publication. Verify the chosen site in Search Console and use dated query reports to choose later topics; no Search Console data is present yet. Do not guarantee rankings or claim a topic is popular until measured.

prompt.label: Analytics event proposal — not active
prompt.text: The repository contains five event definitions in data/shop/measurement.json, explicitly marked PROPOSED because the brief asks for five events but does not name or approve them. Preserve them as a review draft, not live tracking: page_view (page path without query/hash, UTC day, protocol version); outbound_click (path, link host, and only an eligible last path segment; no query string, tag value, full URL, identity or Amazon conversion); guide_view (guide path/day); intent_view (intent-record path/day); flag_view (flagged/publication-pass path/day). The generated browser config currently has enabled=false and endpoint_url empty. The collector is a local script, not a hosted service. No event collection is evidenced.

prompt.label: Privacy and endpoint boundary
prompt.text: GitHub Pages serves static files and its official documentation says visitor IP addresses are logged. The repository includes a local collector prototype, but it is not hosted; counting remains OFF with an empty endpoint URL. A real request-handling runtime is separate. Do not claim privacy-preserving tracking or activate collection until the selected host's actual access/network logs, IP handling, retention, access controls and applicable notice/consent requirements are checked. Do not use cookies, persistent user IDs, fingerprinting, full referrers, query strings or full affiliate URLs. Use authorized Associates reports for order/conversion figures; no user-level Amazon conversion event is available to this page.

prompt.label: Release and compliance gate
prompt.text: Every page must retain the disclosure strip and footer copy; every outbound product link must be sponsored; every table row containing a fact must have an official source link or be explicitly blank/flagged. After any generator or route change, rebuild the feed and sitemap, crawl local links, run all repository compliance checks, and inspect the rendered pages on mobile. No deployment is complete if a gate fails. Keep the dashboard reachable through the one grouped navigation item and footer, not the buyer hero.

design_system.spec: Proposed: warm paper/cream, deep ink, muted sage/olive, one restrained warm accent; keep color roles consistent and test contrast.
design_system.why: A quiet editorial palette makes the product facts and decision actions easier to scan than several competing dashboard colors.

design_system.spec: Editorial serif headlines + high-legibility sans body; body around 17px with relaxed line height, consistent measure and clear caption hierarchy.
design_system.why: Distinct typography creates a publication feel without relying on stock illustrations or decorative clutter.

design_system.spec: One responsive content grid, wide product cards, consistent card padding, generous whitespace and clear section breaks.
design_system.why: The reader should see one decision at a time; avoid dashboard-density and long uninterrupted tables.

design_system.spec: Show official title, category, source date, observed/intent status, one useful buyer question and a clearly labeled direct Amazon link.
design_system.why: A card should help a buyer understand what is known without implying an unverified recommendation.

design_system.spec: Only real owner-created photography with recorded rights or a permitted Amazon-supplied image source; otherwise use original non-photographic diagrams. No generated, copied or scraped product photos.
design_system.why: Image provenance is not present in the five-product register; stay text-first until it is.

design_system.spec: Keep the exact Associates sentence in a high-contrast strip under the masthead on every page, repeat it in the footer and keep it adjacent to recommendations.
design_system.why: This placement is already a site-wide release requirement; visual polish must not hide it.

design_system.spec: Use a clear stacked comparison or horizontally scrollable table with explicit labels, accessible focus and stable disclosure context; never shrink the text to force a wide table.
design_system.why: Readers need to compare without losing product identity or source attribution.

design_system.spec: Use simple, short transitions only; respect prefers-reduced-motion, visible focus and minimum touch target sizing.
design_system.why: A polished shop can still remain accessible and lightweight.

editorial.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
editorial.hook: The shape is the first difference; the listing is only the beginning.
editorial.angle: Compare listed configuration and questions the listing cannot answer.
editorial.fact: The observed titles include a dual-basket fryer, a 26QT French-door oven and an 8Qt basket fryer.
editorial.rule: Do not rank them or infer counter fit, usable capacity or cooking performance.

editorial.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
editorial.hook: A quart number is a label to check, not a serving-size promise.
editorial.angle: Show what capacity is stated and list the measurements a buyer should verify.
editorial.fact: The observed air-fryer listing titles state 6 Quart, 26QT and 8 Qt.
editorial.rule: Do not translate capacity into servings, usable area or family size without a sourced method.

editorial.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
editorial.hook: Separate what the listing says from what the kitchen needs.
editorial.angle: Checklist for dimensions, basket configuration and cleanup details.
editorial.fact: Two observed titles mention dishwasher-safe baskets; the available title observations do not establish all dimensions.
editorial.rule: Do not claim measured footprint, ease of cleaning or countertop fit.

editorial.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
editorial.hook: A preset count is a prompt for questions, not a verdict.
editorial.angle: Explain how to check listed functions, controls and accessories before deciding.
editorial.fact: One observed listing title states 24 one-touch presets and another states a 4-in-1 feature set.
editorial.rule: Do not claim which settings people use or whether they replace other appliances.

editorial.title: What does “two independent baskets” tell you—and what should you still check?
editorial.hook: Two baskets describe a configuration, not a tested dinner plan.
editorial.angle: Unpack the listing terms and give a buyer a verification checklist.
editorial.fact: The observed CHEFMAN title says two independent 3Qt baskets and Sync Finish.
editorial.rule: Do not claim timing, capacity equivalence or cooking results.

editorial.title: What does “dishwasher-safe basket” actually answer?
editorial.hook: The phrase names one part; it does not describe every cleanup step.
editorial.angle: Ask which component is named and what the listing leaves unspecified.
editorial.fact: The observed 6Qt and 8Qt listing titles call out dishwasher-safe baskets.
editorial.rule: Do not claim a tested cleaning result or apply the statement to unmentioned parts.

editorial.title: French-door air fryer oven or basket: which details should you check first?
editorial.hook: Compare form factor and listed controls before comparing adjectives.
editorial.angle: List the factual checks needed before a buyer chooses a countertop format.
editorial.fact: One observed listing title identifies a 26QT French-door multi-function oven; other air-fryer titles describe basket formats.
editorial.rule: Do not infer dimensions, heat distribution or counter-space needs.

editorial.title: Instant-read or wireless meat thermometer: what should you compare?
editorial.hook: The connection type is a starting question, not a performance test.
editorial.angle: Compare listing-stated product form and features; build a checklist for the rest.
editorial.fact: The observed thermometer titles describe one digital meat thermometer and one smart wireless thermometer.
editorial.rule: Do not claim speed, accuracy, connectivity range or cooking outcomes beyond verified official wording.

editorial.title: What do probe count and “wireless” tell you—and what do they not?
editorial.hook: A number or connectivity label is useful only within its stated context.
editorial.angle: Translate listing language into questions a buyer can verify.
editorial.fact: The observed CHEF iQ title states three probes and a wireless feature.
editorial.rule: Do not infer real-world range, battery life or measurement precision.

editorial.title: What should you check on an instant-read thermometer listing?
editorial.hook: Separate the stated specification from a verified test result.
editorial.angle: A source-led checklist for display, stated accuracy language and care instructions.
editorial.fact: The observed ThermoMaven title includes “1 Sec” and an accuracy phrase.
editorial.rule: Do not restate the listing claim as independently tested or certified by this publication.

editorial.title: A pre-holiday kitchen-appliance checklist: what can a listing answer?
editorial.hook: Before the calendar gets busy, check the facts the product page actually states.
editorial.angle: Seasonal editorial hypothesis linking the air-fryer category to listing-reading questions.
editorial.fact: The five observed listings contain different product forms and stated features.
editorial.rule: The seasonal framing is not a popularity claim; no urgency or performance promise.

editorial.title: Before grilling season: which thermometer details should you compare?
editorial.hook: Make a checklist from the listing, not a claim about which device cooks best.
editorial.angle: Seasonal question hypothesis for the two observed thermometer listings.
editorial.fact: The observed thermometer titles describe digital and wireless product forms.
editorial.rule: Do not claim seasonal demand or real-world accuracy without dated evidence and testing.

traffic.what: Use the recommended root + /shop/ + /guides/ information architecture; map unique material from overlapping layers before any redirects.
traffic.why: A clear site structure gives readers and crawlers one coherent publication rather than parallel versions.
traffic.constraint: Do not claim ranking improvement or apply canonical/noindex/redirect changes until routes and links are reviewed.

traffic.what: Answer a buyer question directly, explain the decision trade-off and link to a relevant category/comparison.
traffic.why: The supplied title hypotheses are specific enough to guide useful content without invented trend data.
traffic.constraint: Every factual statement needs an official source; pages must add original explanation relevant to the product link.

traffic.action: Build two topic clusters, not one mixed list
traffic.what: Keep air-fryer questions and thermometer questions in separate category groups; connect to a shared kitchen hub only if it helps a reader.
traffic.why: This reflects the observed five-link scope and makes topical coverage explicit.
traffic.constraint: Category fit is a proposed organization; the owner has not confirmed the wider kitchen niche.

traffic.what: Every article should link to its category pillar, a genuinely relevant comparison and the source/method page.
traffic.why: It helps the reader move from question to decision without adding another microsite.
traffic.constraint: Never create thin pages whose only content is a link list.

traffic.what: Add each approved guide to the existing source/editorial register and rebuild feed.xml and sitemap.xml in the checked chain.
traffic.why: This already automates the publication record and makes omissions detectable.
traffic.constraint: A feed entry or sitemap URL is not evidence of demand or quality.

traffic.action: Measure query data before calling anything popular
traffic.what: After the canonical property is chosen and verified, save dated Search Console query exports and use them to select later topics.
traffic.why: It turns topic choice into an evidence loop rather than a trend guess.
traffic.constraint: No query report is currently recorded; do not promise organic traffic or ranking.

traffic.action: Seasonal content as a dated hypothesis
traffic.what: Use the pre-holiday and grilling-season title ideas only if they fit the chosen audience and can be refreshed by a named editor.
traffic.why: Seasonal framing can make a question timely without claiming the topic is trending.
traffic.constraint: Date each item, name the review/expiry owner, and avoid false scarcity or popularity language.

traffic.what: Record reviewer, source-check date and what changed in each guide; do not publish invented first-person or AI-generated author claims.
traffic.why: A real editorial check is the core difference between a publication and templated listings.
traffic.constraint: No reviewer is currently named; this remains an owner-side gate.

traffic.what: Keep timestamp, report source, channel, eligible sessions, clicks and reported orders only when available from authorized first-party reports or the approved counter.
traffic.why: A dated ledger supports iteration without presenting a modelled conversion score.
traffic.constraint: No current click, conversion, revenue or Search Console figures are entered.

conversion.spec: For each submitted link store intended ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date and source in one block; store observed redirect target/date/source separately.
conversion.why: A redirect is not evidence of requester intent.

conversion.spec: Generate one Special Link for a confirmed intended ASIN in the enrolled workflow; verify the Amazon destination and account report before scaling.
conversion.why: The supplied tag value is not proof of account ownership or a tracked link.

conversion.spec: Use a link label that names Amazon and the listing destination; keep the direct official link, with rel="sponsored".
conversion.why: Readers should know where the action goes; a click tracker must not hide the destination.

conversion.spec: Keep the exact Associates sentence beneath the masthead on every page, repeat it in the footer, and keep the disclosure close to product recommendations.
conversion.why: Disclosure should be visible where the recommendation appears.

conversion.spec: Compare only attributes read from official listing pages; label listing claims as such and keep unknown cells blank/flagged.
conversion.why: A product grid must support a decision without implying tests or unsupported winners.

conversion.spec: Do not show these unless a permitted Amazon-served link or approved API response supplies them under the current program terms.
conversion.why: Static or copied values can go stale and are not available in this build.

conversion.spec: If approved, send a minimal asynchronous event to a separately hosted endpoint while leaving the anchor href unchanged; never add a redirect.
conversion.why: A click counter should not obscure the destination or claim to be an Amazon order.

conversion.spec: Use only aggregate values from authorized Associates first-party reports, with a dated source; do not emit a browser “conversion” event or forecast orders.
conversion.why: The site cannot observe the Amazon checkout itself.

conversion.spec: Do not rank products by commission potential or model revenue while per-product rates, eligible traffic and reports are unverified.
conversion.why: A number without a valid source would give the buyer/operator false confidence.

anti_slop.tell: More than one competing brand or publication front door
anti_slop.fix: Choose one publisher name and canonical page set; keep alternate layers only after a deliberate content map.

anti_slop.tell: Audit counts and policy flags above the buyer decision
anti_slop.fix: Lead with category routes and helpful buyer questions; put governance in one grouped menu and footer.

anti_slop.tell: A listing-title paraphrase presented as a review
anti_slop.fix: Say what the listing states, what was not independently tested, and what the buyer should verify.
Call topics hypotheses; use dated, relevant first-party data before making a popularity statement.

anti_slop.tell: A fake author, first-person testing or invented endorsement
anti_slop.fix: Name a real reviewer only after a real review; otherwise use a transparent editorial label and factual wording.
Use documented original photography or a permitted source; otherwise use original diagrams and typography, not copied/generated product photos.

anti_slop.tell: A table with many blank values that forces a sales-like conclusion
anti_slop.fix: Show only useful verified comparison attributes and flag unknowns in an evidence page.

anti_slop.tell: A generic “Buy now” button or a hidden destination
anti_slop.fix: Name Amazon in the link, show disclosure next to it and use direct sponsored links only after the test gate.

anti_slop.tell: A broken “privacy-preserving analytics” badge or invented conversion number
anti_slop.fix: Keep measurement disabled until an endpoint passes the host/logging review; report orders only from authorized reports.

anti_slop.tell: A decorative article plan that never becomes useful pages
anti_slop.fix: Publish one question-led, human-reviewed guide at the adopted cadence; register, source-check and update its feed/sitemap entry.

workflow: Review the current Questions and Suggestions pages first. They distinguish official facts, repository facts, owner inputs and proposed decisions.
Confirm the five intended products and target marketplace in the enrolled Associates workflow; do not treat the five observed destinations as intent.

After the owner confirms intended ASINs, generate and test one Associates Special Link per product in the enrolled workflow; check each destination and report attribution before changing product CTAs or scaling. Keep submitted short links unchanged and unresolved.
Choose the canonical brand, category scope and route set. Recommended default is root + /shop/ + /guides/; map unique content and inbound links before archiving other layers.
Name a human editor and document the testing and image-rights policy. Do not invent a byline, product test or product photography.
Review the five-event proposal, select an endpoint host and inspect its official logging/retention documentation before any live collection. Keep Amazon orders report-sourced.
Verify the canonical property and collect dated query data before describing a topic as popular or using it as the next editorial signal.
